# EStyle / elk-style-rule

EStyle is a framework-independent, type-safe CSS-in-JS package for TypeScript.
The npm package name is `elk-style-rule`. The main export is the `Estyle` class.
Source repository: https://github.com/ElktrumElk/EStyle
Package documentation: https://github.com/ElktrumElk/EStyle/blob/main/docs/USAGE.md

## Install

`npm install elk-style-rule`

## Import

`import { Estyle } from "elk-style-rule";`

## Primary workflow

1. Create `new Estyle()`.
2. Call `.defineRules({ ruleName: { ...typedCss } })`.
3. Put pseudo, attribute, compound, and descendant selectors in nested keys that
   begin with `&`, for example `"&:hover"` or `"& .icon"`.
4. Optionally call `.defineMedia({ "(max-width: 600px)": { ruleName: {...} } })`.
5. Call `.mount("stable-namespace")` in browser-capable application code.
6. Apply `styles.classes.ruleName` as a class or use
   `styles.rule.ruleName(overrides)` as an inline style object.
7. Call `.destroy()` for dynamically-created sheets.

## Capabilities

- Typed CSS properties through `csstype`
- Stable generated class names
- Hover, active, focus-visible, disabled, and arbitrary safe nested selectors
- Attribute and descendant selectors
- Declarative CSS media queries
- Typed light and dark theme token records
- CSS custom properties
- Server-rendering-safe mounting
- Explicit style element and matchMedia listener cleanup
- No React or other UI framework runtime dependency

## Minimal example

```ts
const styles = new Estyle()
  .defineRules({
    button: {
      color: "white",
      backgroundColor: "#173f36",
      "&:hover": { backgroundColor: "#d75632" },
    },
  })
  .mount("controls");

element.className = styles.classes.button;
```

Use `defineMedia` instead of imperative `mediaQuery` for normal responsive CSS.
Use the `rule` accessor only when an inline style object is needed; nested
selectors are omitted from inline output.
